title: perf(depth): use 2D projective grid traversal in DepthMesh.raycast()
abstract:
# Description

Replaces the brute-force `Mesh.prototype.raycast()` triangle loop in `DepthMesh.raycast()` (~1.18 ms/frame on CPU across 3,042 triangles of `downsampledMesh` × 2 controller rays = 6,084 triangle intersection checks per frame) with a 2D projective grid walk over the depth heightfield in `src/depth/DepthMeshRaycast.ts`:

1. **Per-geometry grid metadata in `DepthGeometryUpdater`**:
   - Tracks `segments`, `isRectilinear`, `minVertexDepth`, `maxVertexDepth`, and `hasDepthData` per geometry when `updateGeometryPositions()` runs, and exposes `getGeometryMetadata()`.
2. **2D projective grid traversal in `DepthMeshRaycaster` (`src/depth/DepthMeshRaycast.ts`)**:
   - Because every vertex of `DepthMesh` lies along its perspective unprojection ray from the camera origin `(0, 0, 0)`, any 3D triangle in grid cell `(ix, iy)` projects under central projection `(x / -z, y / -z)` strictly inside that 2D cell `[ix, ix + 1] × [iy, iy + 1]`, and any 3D ray segment with `-z > 0` projects to a straight 2D line segment in grid space.
   - Clips the local-space ray against the 6 planes of the truncated depth frustum (`zMin`, `zMax`, `rxMin`, `rxMax`, `ryMin`, `ryMax`), projects the entry and exit endpoints into `(c, r)` grid coordinates, and visits only the ~20–40 grid cells crossed by that 2D segment instead of all 1,521 cells.
   - Reads vertex positions directly from the flat `Float32Array` buffer into reusable scratch `THREE.Vector3`s instead of calling `Mesh.getVertexPosition()` 18,252 times per frame.
   - Falls back to standard `Mesh.prototype.raycast()` when depth data has not yet been populated or if a non-rectilinear projection is used.

### On-Device Performance Results (Android XR Chrome Trace)

Measured on-device on `samples/xr_realism/occlusion` (`before_reticle_trace` vs `after_reticle_trace`):

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| **`DepthMesh.raycast`** | **1.177 ms/frame** | **0.072 ms/frame** | **-93.9% (`16.3×` faster, `-1.105 ms/f`)** |
| **`collectIntersections` (Scene Raycast)** | 1.292 ms/frame | **0.187 ms/frame** | **-85.5% (`6.9×` faster, `-1.105 ms/f`)** |
| **`InteractionManager.updateRay`** | 1.538 ms/frame | **0.407 ms/frame** | **-73.5% (`-1.131 ms/f`)** |
| **`Core.update` Total** | 5.189 ms/frame | **4.327 ms/frame** | **-16.6% (`-0.862 ms/f`)** |
| **`onAnimationFrame` CPU (mean)** | 5.88 ms | **4.82 ms** | **-18.0% (`-1.06 ms/f`)** |
| **`onAnimationFrame` CPU (median / p90)** | 5.69 / 6.84 ms | **4.54 / 5.91 ms** | **-20.2% / -13.6%** |
| **Main-Thread `RunTask` Total** | 7.21 ms/frame (51.7% busy) | **6.22 ms/frame (44.2% busy)** | **-13.7% (`-0.99 ms/f`)** |

# Test Plan

- Automated unit tests (`npm test`):
  - Added tests in `src/depth/DepthMesh.test.ts` verifying that `DepthMesh.raycast()` returns identical intersection points, distances, face indices, normals, and `.object === depthMesh` references as Three.js's brute-force `Mesh.prototype.raycast` across centered, angled, diagonal, grazing multi-hit, and miss rays with a non-trivial world pose.
- Verified on-device with Chrome DevTools Performance traces on Android XR (`samples/xr_realism/occlusion`).
